clue.text: Company colleague blocked by penny-pincher — show sympathy

indicators.note: the colleague word is obstructed, with the penny-pincher wedged in its middle

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague
a miser is a stingy penny-pincher

explanation.surface: A firm's employee gets stopped by a skinflint, and someone else offers comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To commiserate is to express pity or condolence to someone in trouble.

clue.text: American resort region occupying golden ring

indicators.note: the region sits within, filling the space between the golden and ring letters

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
O is ring-shaped
a land is a country or region

explanation.surface: A US holiday area takes up a gilded circle of land.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city is a famous holiday destination with theme parks.

clue.text: Religious follower encountered lots of people around day one

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, to encounter

indicators.note: the crowd word goes round the day and one letters

parts.note: a host is a great multitude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A churchgoer met a crowd around the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts DI inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Wesleyan Protestant denomination are adherents of a faith.

clue.text: Sweet stuff, surely without content, and not entirely wholesome on reflection

indicators.note: surely with its insides emptied leaves only its first and last letters
reflected as in a mirror, the shortened word is read backwards
the wholesome word loses its final letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: pure means wholesome, untainted

explanation.surface: Something sugary that is surely hollow and hardly healthy, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: SY is surely emptied; PURE less its last letter is PUR, and 'on reflection' turns it to RUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrup is a thick sugary liquid, a classic sweet thing.

clue.text: French is adopted by group not in a show?

indicators.note: the French word is taken into the group word

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A French word is taken up by a company of players who are between shows.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor between jobs is euphemistically 'resting', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-of-work actors are said to be resting when they have no engagement.

clue.text: A good deal alarmed about hollow drums

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the hollow word
only a good deal of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: timid means fearful, easily alarmed
a pan is a hollow or depression in the ground, as in a salt pan

explanation.surface: Much alarmed about drums that sound empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal alarmed' reads as one phrase but splits; 'hollow' is a noun here, not an adjective for the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums of an orchestra are collectively known by this Italian plural.

clue.text: Sports event for everyone to see in remarkable camera pics

indicators.note: the certificate letter goes inside the rearranged letters
remarkable here means remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A sporting occasion that all can watch, captured in striking photos.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal audiences; 'in' puts it inside an anagram of CAMERA PICS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous international yachting trophy and race series.

clue.text: Free up new length to secure daughter's skirt

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: the new and length letters hold the daughter letter between them

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; the possessive points to the skirt as hers

explanation.surface: Loosening a fresh length to hold the girl's skirt in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RID; N and L 'secure' D between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirndl is a full, gathered Alpine-style skirt.

clue.text: Swimsuit showing letters and large number

parts.note: mail is letters through the post
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: A bathing costume revealed through a pile of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a one-piece bathing costume, from the French.

clue.text: About to receive inspiration when going over CV

indicators.note: the about word takes in the turned word between its two letters

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the inspiration word is read backwards

parts.note: a muse is a source of inspiration

explanation.surface: Getting a bright idea while reviewing a job application document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when going over' turns MUSE to ESUM, which RE 'receives'. 'going over CV' looks like reading it, but the CV is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a curriculum vitae a résumé, a summary of career history.

clue.text: One's measures are derived from wood (axes cut this on being swung)

definitions.text: One's measures are derived from wood

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph
to lop is to cut

indicators.note: the letters are swung about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodsman's lumber derives from timber felled by swinging axes.
explanation.walkthrough: XY are the graph axes; 'being swung' scrambles LOP and THISON. 'Measures' are musical bars, here literally wooden.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the instrument whose tuned bars are wooden produces musical measures from wood.

clue.text: Come across several performances — very keen on following them

indicators.note: the keen word comes after the performances word

parts.note: a run is a series of performances of a show
to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it

explanation.surface: Meeting by chance at a string of shows one is enthusiastic about.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, an idiom.

clue.text: Snoop capturing one blemish in school

indicators.note: the snoop word takes the other letters prisoner inside it

parts.note: to pry is to snoop
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mar is a flaw or blemish

explanation.surface: A nosy person catches someone with a spot at school.
explanation.definitionFit: An elementary school for young children is a primary in Britain.

clue.text: Chamber group's core instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small room or chamber

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A chamber ensemble's central instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber group' reads as a musical ensemble but splits: CELL plus the middle of 'group'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Fashionable company attempt to keep fool's name unknown

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the attempt word holds the fool inside it

parts.note: a go is an attempt
a nit is a fool; the apostrophe-s is read as is

explanation.surface: A trendy firm tries to conceal an idiot's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling under a hidden identity, their name not disclosed, goes incognito.

clue.text: Alcohol money mostly to pay for university

parts.note: coin is cash, money

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to treat someone is to pay for them

explanation.surface: Cash largely used to fund a student's studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TREAT to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a type of spirit.

clue.text: I will follow argument about good mix of ingredients for the food

indicators.note: the I comes after everything else
the argument word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a spat is a minor argument

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are the ingredients to be mixed

explanation.surface: A cook's quarrel over a good blend of ingredients for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like an article before 'food' but is the fodder for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple dish.

clue.text: A measure of speed or a measure of liquid

parts.note: mph is miles per hour

explanation.surface: A list of options between units of velocity and volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient two-handled jar also served as a standard unit of capacity for wine or oil.

clue.text: That chap haplessly led around following United should be paying attention

parts.note: he refers to a man, that chap

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the following and United letters
haplessly means in a muddled, unlucky way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A man clumsily led a United fan who ought to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haplessly' rearranges LED to EDL, which goes 'around' FU.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedful means taking notice, attentive.

clue.text: Patch left from discoloration

indicators.note: the left letter is removed from the discoloration word

parts.note: a blotch is a discoloured mark

explanation.surface: A mark remains after a stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patch' looks like a noun for a stain but is the verb: to mend clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch is to repair something clumsily, a careless patching job.

clue.text: Country's reduced propensity to consume a lot of fruit

definitions.note: the possessive with the cryptic link reads as 'country is'

indicators.note: the shortened propensity word swallows the shortened fruit
the propensity word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a bias is an inclination or propensity

indicators.note: most of the fruit word is used, its final letter lost

parts.note: an olive is a fruit

explanation.surface: A nation's diminished appetite for eating heaps of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts BIAS to BIA; 'a lot of' cuts OLIVE to OLIV, which BIA 'consumes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American nation.

clue.text: Stand up to perform after stumble

indicators.note: the perform word comes after the stumble word

parts.note: a trip is a stumble

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Getting up to do one's act after falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' looks like one verb, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or similar.

clue.text: An unspecified number giving support to politician in international body

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the international body

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: the support word is given to the politician, placed after it

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Many backing a politician at the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for very many, an indefinite large quantity.

clue.text: Impressively turned on by embracing lady at the outset

indicators.note: turned round, the little word is read backwards
the word by holds the initial letter in its arms
at the outset means the very start of the word lady

explanation.surface: Greatly aroused by holding a woman from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting nobly means acting in a grand, admirable manner.

clue.text: British author to tell stories about King and knight

indicators.note: the lying word goes around the king letter

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A writer is set to spin yarns of monarchs and chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts K inside LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: J.R.R. Tolkien was the English writer of The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Not supporting wicked chat

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
wicked is slang for excellent, as is fab

explanation.surface: Opposition to a nasty conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is slang praise, not villainy.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal conversation, short for confabulation.

clue.text: Resentful and unscrupulous, seizing note daughter dropped

indicators.note: the shortened word grabs the note letter inside it
the daughter letter is let fall from the unscrupulous word

parts.note: devious means underhand, unscrupulous

explanation.surface: A bitter, underhand person snatching a message once the girl leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes D from DEVIOUS, giving EVIOUS, which is 'seizing' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous covetousness of what others have is to feel resentful.

clue.text: Sucker's drawn to this by a regular's fooling

definitions.note: a sweet you suck attracts anyone who sucks; the gullible sense of sucker misleads

indicators.note: fooling around, the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A gullible person is lured in by a regular customer's trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a dupe but means someone sucking a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley sugar is a hard, twisted boiled sweet for sucking.
